label: Adapted historical materialism into feminist standpoint sociology
description: Dorothy Smith drew upon Marx and Engels's German Ideology to ground sociology not in ideological abstractions, but in the actual embodied activities and material labor of everyday life.
dialecticalTension: Extends Marxian critique of alienated labor to unpaid domestic work and textualized bureaucratic power.
historicalContext: Formulated in The Everyday World as Problematic (1987).

citations.author: Dorothy E. Smith
citations.work: The Everyday World as Problematic: A Feminist Sociology

label: Informed embodied phenomenology of the situated sociological subject
description: Smith synthesized Merleau-Ponty's phenomenology of embodied perception with ethnomethodology to show how knowing always begins from a specific bodily location in the material world.
dialecticalTension: Counters disembodied 'Archimedean' sociology with embodied phenomenological presence.
historicalContext: Integrated across Smith's Institutional Ethnography methodology (1987–2005).

citations.author: Dorothy E. Smith
citations.work: Institutional Ethnography: A Sociology for People

label: Mentored Smith's micro-sociological attention to everyday institutional order
description: Trained at UC Berkeley where Goffman taught, Smith built upon Goffmanian micro-sociology while expanding it to map how local interactions are coordinated by trans-local textual relations of ruling.
dialecticalTension: Connects micro-interactional order to macro-institutional structures of gendered and class power.
historicalContext: Berkeley sociological formation (1960s) transformed into feminist institutional ethnography.

label: Founded feminist standpoint sociology and institutional ethnography
description: Smith demonstrated that orthodox sociology's objective gaze reproduced a bifurcated consciousness, and designed institutional ethnography to trace how texts coordinate people's everyday work.
dialecticalTension: Replaces detached theoretical categorization with empirically mapped relations of ruling.
historicalContext: Inaugurated in 'Women's Perspective as a Radical Critique of Sociology' (1974) and The Everyday World as Problematic (1987).

citations.author: Elizabeth Anderson
citations.work: Feminist Epistemology and Philosophy of Science

label: Catalyzed sociological standpoint theory extended into Black feminist epistemology
description: Patricia Hill Collins engaged Smith's critique of objectified sociological knowledge to articulate how Black women's 'outsider within' location generates distinct intersectional standpoint insights.
dialecticalTension: Expands standpoint methodology from gender-and-class bifurcation to interlocking racial, class, and gender oppression.
historicalContext: Cross-pollination of feminist standpoint theory during the 1980s–1990s.
